title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Reference, Day‑2 Ops, and Upgrade/Rollback Playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments, covering VPC deployment patterns, on‑prem packaging and air‑gap installs, reference architectures, day‑2 operations (monitoring, scaling, backups), and detailed upgrade/rollback procedures. It also includes a customer requirements library and checklists that SEs and solutions architects can use during scoping and handoffs.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Solutions Engineers, Platform/Infra Engineers, Customer SREs, and Security/Compliance reviewers.
- Scope: Production deployments of Redwood Private (VPC and on‑prem), including initial install, network/security prerequisites, operational runbooks for day‑2, and safe upgrade/rollback workflows.

Owner and contact:
- Doc owner: Maya Patel (Platform Solutions).
- Primary engineering owners: eng-private-deployments team.
- Support contacts: private-deployments@redwood.ai, oncall-eng-private (PagerDuty).

Prerequisites and assumptions:
1) Customer has executed the Customer Requirements Questionnaire (see "Customer requirements checklist" section).
2) Networking: CIDR blocks, peering, and routing will be agreed and documented in the project brief.
3) For GPU workloads, validated node types with correct driver versions must be available.
4) Customers requiring HSM/KMS integrations must provide test/staging credentials in advance and have approved firewall rules.

High‑level architecture components (terms used throughout):
- control-plane: Redwood management/control components (runs either in Redwood cloud or in customer VPC for Private control plane).
- node-agent: host agent responsible for lifecycle hooks and local telemetry.
- runtime: GPU/CPU inference runtime (containerized components performing model serving).
- model-store: blob/object storage used for storing model artifacts and quantized variants.
- kv-cache: optional Redis/managed cache for prefix/KV cache persistence.
- telemetry: metrics/traces shipped to customer observability endpoint or to Redwood Console (per contract).

Reference architectures (choose based on scale and regulatory needs):
1) Small customer (dev/test up to 4 GPUs)
   - Single private VPC, 2 subnets (control, compute), 3 worker nodes (1 control, 2 worker), model-store in S3-compatible object storage.
   - Storage: 1TB as default, increase based on model catalog.
   - Use host‑based NVMe for kv-cache.

2) Production (dedicated inference fleet, 8‑64 GPUs)
   - Multi‑AZ VPC with private subnets per AZ; autoscaling group across AZs.
   - Managed Redis for durable KV cache; S3/Buckets for model-store; EFS/NFS only if required for shared state.
   - Control plane components deployed in a private subnet with restricted egress; explicit peering with Redwood control (if hybrid).

3) Regulated/Air‑gapped on‑prem
   - Air‑gapped bundle (OCI images, Helm charts offline), local object store (MinIO or customer object store), local KMS or HSM integration.
   - Strict ingress/egress rules; all telemetry kept on prem unless otherwise contracted.

Network and security requirements (VPC deployments):
- Subnets: allocate dedicated subnets for control-plane, runtime, and storage. Example: 10.10.0.0/24 control, 10.10.1.0/22 compute, 10.10.5.0/24 storage.
- Security groups: allow only required ports between components. Minimum port list:
  - 443/TCP: control-plane API (TLS)
  - 2379/TCP: etcd (if self‑hosted; restrict to control-plane CIDR)
  - 6379/TCP: Redis (restrict to runtime CIDR)
  - 10250/TCP: kubelet (if Kubernetes managed)
  - 50051/TCP: runtime gRPC control channel (internal)
- NAT/egress: Control plane may need egress for package updates and image pulls; in Restricted deployments use image registry mirror in customer network.
- IAM: principle of least privilege. Provide example IAM roles for AWS:
  - redwood-private-node-role: S3 read, KMS decrypt, CloudWatch put-metrics (if applicable).

Storage and model distribution:
- Recommended: S3-compatible object store (MinIO or cloud S3). Models should be sharded across folders by model-version.
- Model cache policy: keep hot models on local NVMe with LRU eviction. Minimum buffer: 20% free space.
- Example model-store layout: /models/{model_name}/{version}/{artifact}.pt or .onnx

On‑prem packaging and air‑gap install:
- Deliverables in air‑gapped bundle:
  - OCI tarballs of Redwood runtime images and utilities
  - Helm charts and CRDs (packaged)
  - Installation scripts (bash) and an offline image registry manifest
  - Documentation and preflight scripts
- Host requirements (per node):
  - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or RHEL 8.6
  - Container runtime: containerd 1.7+ or Docker 24+ (secure config)
  - GPU drivers: NVIDIA driver 525+ and NVIDIA Container Toolkit matching the driver
  - Disk: 2TB recommended (1TB model cache + OS + logs).
- Installer flow (air‑gap):
  1) Mirror images into local registry using provided manifests.
  2) Apply CRDs and Helm charts from packaged release.
  3) Configure model-store endpoint and KMS/HSM connection strings.
  4) Start control-plane and runtime, validate with smoke tests.

Day‑2 operations (monitoring, scaling, and maintenance):
- Observability:
  - Metrics required: request latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization per card, model cache hit rate, error rate per route.
  - Recommended exporters: node_exporter, nvidia_dcgm_exporter for GPU metrics, redis_exporter.
  - Dashboards: one per model family with latency buckets and cost breakdown (tokens * cost/unit).
- Alerts (recommended thresholds):
  - Latency P95 > 2x baseline for 10m → P1 (investigate model or runtime throttling).
  - GPU memory pressure > 90% → P2 (scale up or evict models).
  - Model cache hit rate < 60% → P3 (review hot models & prefetch).
- Scaling:
  - For autoscaling with batch-aware policy: scale when queue depth > 1000 or average latency exceeds configured SLO.
  - Batching knobs: target batch size 16‑64 depending on model; adjust based on latency SLO (SLOs are application specific).
- Backups and disaster recovery:
  - Snapshot model-store metadata daily; replicate model artifacts to a cold store.
  - Backup Redis RDB or AOF per vendor best practice; keep 7-day retention by default.
- Patching and CVE management:
  - Monthly node OS patch window; test a canary AZ/node first.
  - Image rotation: publish fixed image tags; avoid rolling images with :latest in production.

Upgrade and rollback procedures (safe pattern):
1) Pre‑upgrade checks (always run):
   - Validate cluster health: all Pods Ready, no CrashLoopBackOff.
   - Ensure model-store and kv-cache reachable and under baseline load.
   - Take metadata snapshot and store in versioned S3 path.
   - Run smoke tests against existing control-plane and runtime.

2) Canary upgrade (recommended):
   - Deploy new control-plane components to 1 AZ / 1 replica with feature flags disabled.
   - Route 1‑5% of traffic to the canary using ingress or weighted routing.
   - Monitor latency, error rates, model correctness for 30‑60 minutes.

3) Rolling upgrade (if canary healthy):
   - Upgrade control-plane and node‑agent using maxUnavailable: 1 (K8s strategy) or rolling restart policy.
   - Upgrade runtime on a per-node basis: cordon node → drain non-critical pods → update daemonset/statefulset → uncordon.
   - After each AZ, validate smoke tests and SLOs.

4) Post‑upgrade validation:
   - Run full regression prompts (sample prompt sets for top 10 routes).
   - Confirm model cache warming (model caches repopulated) and verify hit rate returns to baseline within configured warmup window.

5) Rollback plan (if failure):
   - Trigger immediate traffic cutover to previous stable control-plane via weighted routing or DNS TTL change.
   - Execute Helm rollback to previous release tag for control-plane and runtime.
   - Restore metadata snapshot if migrations failed.
   - Run incident triage runbook and capture diagnostics (logs, traces, core dumps).

Upgrade safety checklist (short):
- [ ] snapshot metadata
- [ ] confirm backups for model-store and cache
- [ ] reserve maintenance window and notify customers
- [ ] validate canary tests and rollback playbook

Customer requirements library (scoping checklist):
- Networking: VPC CIDRs, public/private subnets, NAT/egress policy, peering required, ports allowed.
- Security: KMS/HSM, SIEM/Log forwarder endpoint, RBAC requirements, secrets management method.
- Compute: preferred instance types and GPU SKUs; minimum GPUs per AZ.
- Storage: preferred object store, throughput and IOPS needs, retention policy.
- Compliance: required certifications (SOC2, FedRAMP, ISO27001), data residency, audit logging.
- Deployment cadence: expected weekly vs monthly upgrades, maintenance windows.
- Observability: target retention for metrics/traces/logs and endpoints for exporters.

Operational runbooks (links and summaries):
- Incident: High GPU saturation → Scale policy runbook (cordon/drain/add-nodes).
- Incident: Control-plane unavailable → Failover to standby control-plane and rollback.
- Routine: Model eviction and cache cleanup (scripted job run weekly).

Troubleshooting quick hits:
- Slow responses with low GPU utilization: check batching config and queue depth; investigate KV-cache hit rate.
- Memory OOM on runtime: check model artifacts size and quantization profile; consider loading quantized variants.
- High error rate after upgrade: compare request/response diffs using trace IDs and sample prompts; mark for regression.

Appendix: example commands and config snippets
- Helm install (VPC):
  helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood.ai/stable
  helm install redwood-private redwood/private --namespace redwood --set modelStore.endpoint=https://minio.example.internal --set node.agent.enabled=true

- Offline image mirror (air‑gap):
  ctr images import redwood-runtime_v1.2.3.tar
  registryctl push local-registry redwood-runtime:v1.2.3

- Sample smoke test (curl):
  curl -k -X POST https://private-api.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"r-instruct-1","input":"Hello"}'

Related documentation:
- See: private-deployments-playbook-2026 for operational checklists.
- See: private-deployments-day2-upgrade-rollback-2026 for a step‑by‑step upgrade runbook.

Appendix B: SLO suggestions (for customer contract negotiation)
- Latency SLO: P95 < 500ms for small models, P95 < 1.5s for large context models (>8k tokens) under nominal load.
- Availability SLO: 99.9% for control-plane; 99.5% for model-serving for most enterprise tiers (adjust per contract).

Revision history and notes:
- 2025-11-10: Created initial draft.
- 2026-01-08: Added air‑gap packaging details and GPU driver matrix.
- 2026-02-20: Expanded upgrade/rollback procedures and added customer requirements checklist.

If you have a customer-specific scenario (non‑standard networking, legacy NFS requirements, HSM integration details), open a ticket in the private-deployments backlog and attach the customer questionnaire export.
